HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Colonial Administration in Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Colonial Administration in Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Say Colonial Administration in Africa never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Colonial Administration in Africa.
   D. Treat Colonial Administration in Africa as rumours only.

2. Which statement about Internal conflicts in Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Internal conflicts in Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Internal conflicts in Africa as rumours only.
   C. Say Internal conflicts in Africa never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Internal conflicts in Africa.

3. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Measure rainfall only
   B. Name the president
   C. Replace the compass rose
   D. Explain symbols used on a map

4. Which statement about Kenyans Response to Colonialism is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Kenyans Response to Colonialism with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Kenyans Response to Colonialism.
   C. Say Kenyans Response to Colonialism never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Kenyans Response to Colonialism as rumours only.

5. Which statement about National Security is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say National Security never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing National Security.
   C. Explain National Security with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Treat National Security as rumours only.

6. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Nakuru
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nairobi

7. Which statement about Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya.
   B. Explain Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Say Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya as rumours only.

8. Which statement about Civilisations in South and Central Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Civilisations in South and Central Africa.
   B. Treat Civilisations in South and Central Africa as rumours only.
   C. Explain Civilisations in South and Central Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Say Civilisations in South and Central Africa never happens in Kenya.

9. Which statement about Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya as rumours only.
   B. Explain Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya.
   D. Say Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya never happens in Kenya.

10. Which statement about Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century.
   B. Treat Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century as rumours only.
   C. Explain Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Say Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century never happens in Kenya.

11. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Hide all money underground
   B. Avoid saving forever
   C. Plan income and spending wisely
   D. Ignore prices in shops

12. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Avoiding all community work
   B. Littering in markets
   C. Obeying laws and caring for public property
   D. Destroying road signs

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyans Response to Colonialism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Explain Colonial Administration in Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

2. A — Explain Internal conflicts in Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. D — Explain symbols used on a map

4. A — Explain Kenyans Response to Colonialism with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. C — Explain National Security with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

6. D — Nairobi

7. B — Explain Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

8. C — Explain Civilisations in South and Central Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

9. B — Explain Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

10. C — Explain Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

11. C — Plan income and spending wisely

12. C — Obeying laws and caring for public property

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyans Response to Colonialism; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Public Resources under the Constitution of Kenya; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
